speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have experienced episodes of unresponsiveness accompanied by facial grimacing. To better understand your condition, can you tell me exactly how long these episodes typically last?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Absence Status Epilepticus (likely evolving from childhood absence seizures). The duration of 3–4 minutes with post-ictal lethargy and confusion suggests this is not typical brief absence seizures, but rather a more prolonged form requiring urgent management. REQUEST TEST: EEG; REQUEST IMAGES: None at this stage.
